statement: Every dart on a board scores 1, 3, 5 or 7 points. Lea throws three darts and all of them hit the board. Which total could she score?

choices.misconception: I used 3 + 3 = 6 and forgot that Lea throws a third dart.
I used 2 + 3 + 3 = 8 without checking which scores are on the board.
I used 5 + 5 = 10, which is only two darts.
I used 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 without checking which scores are on the board.

hints: Are the scores on the board odd or even?
Every score on the board is odd. Think about what happens to odd and even when you add two odd numbers, and then add one more odd number.
Odd + odd is even, and even + odd is odd. So three odd scores always add to an odd total. Which choice is odd, and can you make it?

solutions.reliable: Every score is odd. Two odd numbers add to an even number, and adding a third odd number makes the total odd again. So three darts always give an odd total. Only 13 is odd, and 7 + 5 + 1 = 13 shows it can really happen. The idea to keep: add odd numbers in pairs, since each pair is even, and one left over makes the total odd.
solutions.elegant: Each odd score is an even number plus 1. Three darts give three of those extra 1s, which is 3, and 3 is odd, so the total is odd. Then check 13 = 7 + 5 + 1. The idea to keep: count the leftover 1s to decide odd or even.

whyOnTest: Parity lets a student rule out four choices without trying a single sum, and still check that the last one really works.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
